title: CRT ASCII
look: A green phosphor terminal: the character drawn in text-mode glyphs, scanlines, a blinking prompt.

doc.essence: ASCII art on a monochrome monitor: every area is filled with character cells whose glyph gets denser the brighter the area, glowing green behind the glass.
doc.notIt: Not pixel (one green, text cells instead of colour pixels), not one-bit (glowing green on black, glyphs not dither), not synthwave (no neon gradient, no sun).
doc.shapes: A thin phosphor edge on each part. Inside, a grid of 5 by 7 cells, each holding one glyph: a dot, a plus, a hash or a full block.
doc.colour: Only green phosphor in four brightnesses on a near-black screen. Brighter areas get heavier glyphs.
doc.eyes: The brightest phosphor, solid, like a cursor block.
doc.motion: Redraws at 15 fps, like a slow terminal.
pitfalls: Two areas of the same lightness get the same glyph: the edge keeps them apart.
Scanlines over the eyes must stay faint.
